statements.text:
The Global Engagement Center at the State Department was formed to counter the messaging and diminish the influence of international terrorist organizations.

The termination of this center creates a void in combatting disinformation and propaganda that will only worsen with the evolution of AI. 

During today’s hearing, I talked about the need for Democrats and Republicans to put partisanship aside to protect our nation and our influence around the world.

I enjoyed speaking at @POLITICO's Health Care Summit to discuss the integration of AI into our health care system. 

As a doctor, I’ve seen how the right tools can improve patient outcomes and reduce provider burnout. AI holds real promise—but Congress must act to ensure we have the right safeguards in place. 

Last Congress, I served on the House Bipartisan Task Force on AI, which released a report outlining key opportunities and challenges for responsible AI use. It’s important we build on that work. 

We need thoughtful, bipartisan solutions to ensure that AI is deployed as a force for good in health care.

Decisions about exporting our most advanced AI chips shouldn’t be made unilaterally behind closed doors. This bill reasserts Congress’ authority and ensures that any such transfer to the People’s Republic of China is subject to full scrutiny. Our national security demands a deliberate and lawful process, not ad hoc deals that risk handing over our technological edge to the PRC.

Pediatric cancer remains one of the most heartbreaking diagnoses any family can face, and we have a responsibility to use every tool available to improve outcomes for children. statements.text:
Yesterday, I joined more than 100 of my colleagues urging Speaker Johnson to keep the House in session to address the growing risks posed by AI.

Instead of taking action, Speaker Johnson announced that he’s sending us home early for seven weeks.

AI isn’t slowing down. Neither should we. We must remain in Washington to advance meaningful, bipartisan safeguards that meet this moment with the urgency it demands.

Ahead of the Trump-Xi summit next week, I led a letter with @RepGregoryMeeks and @RepSaraJacobs urging senior administration officials to engage in sustained and substantive dialogue with China to address AI-related safety risks. https://t.co/2dicGeIhTQ

statements.text:
Today is the third annual National App Challenge Day!

The Congressional App Challenge is a unique opportunity for middle and high school students across Sacramento County to showcase their STEM skills and represent our district on the national stage.

Earlier this year, I had the chance to welcome our 2025 Congressional App Challenge winners, Aarit Atreja and Anvi Atreja, to my Washington, D.C. office. 

These talented students from Davis Senior High School and Oliver Wendell Holmes Junior High School developed Learn AI, an interactive educational app that helps people of all ages become more AI literate.

This was another unproductive week in Mike Johnson’s House of Representatives.

The Speaker canceled votes and sent us home for seven weeks to avoid an impeachment vote on Secretary Hegseth.

We still have too much work to do, from confronting rising AI threats to addressing the affordability crisis, for Congress to leave town. 

The American people deserve a Congress that actually does its job.

This report must be a wake-up call. The United States and China need reliable crisis communication channels and serious dialogue on AI guardrails before a mistake like this becomes a disaster.

That means establishing clear guardrails for the use of AI across the U.S. military and Intelligence Community, ensuring critical intelligence is carefully verified before decisions are made, and creating mechanisms to deconflict during a crisis. 

During the Cold War, Washington and Moscow understood the importance of direct communication in moments of heightened tension. We need similar channels with Beijing today.
